dsaQuestions.title: Two Sum
dsaQuestions.description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. You may assume each input has exactly one solution.
dsaQuestions.hint: Use a Hash Map to store previously visited elements and their indices for O(n) lookup.

dsaQuestions.title: Maximum Subarray (Kadane's Algorithm)
dsaQuestions.description: Given an integer array nums, find the subarray with the largest sum, and return its sum.
dsaQuestions.hint: Maintain currentSum and maxSum. If currentSum drops below 0, reset it to 0.

dsaQuestions.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
dsaQuestions.description: You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the ith day. Maximize your profit by choosing a single day to buy and a different day in the future to sell.
dsaQuestions.hint: Track minPrice seen so far and calculate max profit for each day.

dsaQuestions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
dsaQuestions.description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
dsaQuestions.hint: Use Sliding Window technique with a Set or Map storing the latest character indices.

dsaQuestions.title: Valid Palindrome
dsaQuestions.description: A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward.
dsaQuestions.hint: Clean non-alphanumeric chars with regex, then use two pointers moving inwards.

dsaQuestions.title: Reverse a Linked List
dsaQuestions.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list, and return the reversed list.
dsaQuestions.hint: Keep three pointers: prev = null, curr = head, and nextNode.

dsaQuestions.title: Detect Cycle in Linked List
dsaQuestions.description: Given head, the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it using Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm.
dsaQuestions.hint: Fast pointer moves 2 steps, slow pointer moves 1 step. If they meet, a cycle exists.

dsaQuestions.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
dsaQuestions.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (i.e., from left to right, level by level).
dsaQuestions.hint: Use Breadth-First Search (BFS) with a queue. Process level size in each iteration.

dsaQuestions.title: Invert Binary Tree
dsaQuestions.description: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree (mirror image), and return its root.
dsaQuestions.hint: Recursively swap left and right subtrees for each node.

dsaQuestions.title: Climbing Stairs
dsaQuestions.description: You are climbing a staircase. It takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you climb to the top?
dsaQuestions.hint: Ways(n) = Ways(n-1) + Ways(n-2). This is equivalent to Fibonacci numbers.

dsaQuestions.title: 0/1 Knapsack Problem
dsaQuestions.description: Given weights and values of n items, put these items in a knapsack of capacity W to get maximum total value in the knapsack.

dsaQuestions.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
dsaQuestions.description: Given the array nums sorted in ascending order (with distinct values) and rotated at an unknown pivot, return the index of target, or -1 if not found in O(log n).
dsaQuestions.hint: In any rotated sorted array, at least one half (left or right) is strictly sorted. Check if target lies within the sorted half.

quizzes.question: A train running at 54 km/hr takes 20 seconds to cross a platform 150 meters long. What is the length of the train?
quizzes.explanation: Speed = 54 * (5/18) = 15 m/s. Total distance in 20s = 15 * 20 = 300m. Train length = Total distance - Platform length = 300 - 150 = 150m.

quizzes.question: If 'CODING' is coded as 'DPEJOH', what is the code for 'CAMPUS'?
quizzes.explanation: Each letter is shifted by +1: C->D, A->B, M->N, P->Q, U->V, S->T. Result = DBNQVT.

quizzes.question: A can finish a work in 12 days and B can finish it in 24 days. Working together, in how many days can they finish the work?
quizzes.explanation: 1/A + 1/B = 1/12 + 1/24 = 3/24 = 1/8. Together they finish the work in 8 days.

quizzes.question: Which normal form removes transitive dependencies?
quizzes.explanation: Third Normal Form (3NF) ensures the table is in 2NF and no non-prime attribute is transitively dependent on the primary key.

quizzes.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the Coffman conditions for a deadlock to occur?
quizzes.explanation: No preemption is a required Coffman condition. If preemption is allowed, deadlock cannot occur.

quizzes.question: Which protocol works at the Transport layer and provides reliable, connection-oriented data transfer?
quizzes.explanation: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is connection-oriented, guarantees delivery, error checking, and ordering at Layer 4.

quizzes.question: Method overloading is an example of which type of polymorphism?
quizzes.explanation: Method overloading is resolved at compile time based on method signatures, hence Compile-time polymorphism.

quizzes.question: Pointing to a photograph of a boy, Suresh said, 'He is the son of the only son of my mother.' How is Suresh related to that boy?
quizzes.explanation: The 'only son of Suresh's mother' is Suresh himself. Therefore, the boy is Suresh's son, making Suresh the Father.

concepts.title: ACID Properties
concepts.summary: Atomicity (all or nothing), Consistency (preserves invariants), Isolation (concurrent transactions don't interfere), Durability (committed changes persist even after crashes).

concepts.title: Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF)
concepts.summary: 1NF: Atomic values; 2NF: No partial dependency on composite key; 3NF: No transitive dependency; BCNF: For every functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a super key.

concepts.title: SQL vs NoSQL Databases
concepts.summary: SQL (PostgreSQL, MySQL) are relational, table-based, strict schema, ACID-compliant. NoSQL (MongoDB, Redis) are non-relational, document/key-value based, horizontally scalable.

concepts.title: Indexing (B-Trees / B+ Trees)
concepts.summary: Data structures that improve speed of data retrieval operations on a table at the cost of additional writes and storage space. B+ Trees keep all data in leaf nodes.

concepts.title: Process vs Thread
concepts.summary: A process is an execution instance with its own address space, memory, and file handles. A thread is a lightweight execution unit inside a process sharing the same address space.

concepts.title: Deadlock & Coffman Conditions
concepts.summary: A state where a set of processes are blocked waiting for resources held by each other. 4 Conditions: Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait.

concepts.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms
concepts.summary: FCFS (First Come First Serve), SJF (Shortest Job First), Round Robin (time quantum-based, fair for timesharing), Priority Scheduling.

concepts.title: Virtual Memory & Paging
concepts.summary: Technique allowing execution of processes not completely in physical memory. Divides logical memory into Pages and physical memory into Frames with a Page Table mapping.

concepts.title: OSI 7 Layers vs TCP/IP 4 Layers
concepts.summary: OSI: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application. TCP/IP: Network Interface, Internet, Transport, Application.

concepts.title: TCP vs UDP
concepts.summary: TCP: Connection-oriented, reliable, ordering guaranteed, flow & congestion control (HTTP, Email). UDP: Connectionless, fast, no delivery guarantees (DNS, Video Streaming, Gaming).

concepts.title: TCP 3-Way Handshake
concepts.summary: Client sends SYN -> Server responds with SYN-ACK -> Client replies with ACK. Establishes sequence numbers and connection state.

concepts.title: DNS & What Happens When You Type a URL
concepts.summary: Browser cache check -> OS cache -> Resolving Name Server -> Root -> TLD -> Authoritative NS -> IP returned -> TCP 3-way handshake -> TLS handshake -> HTTP GET -> HTML rendered.

concepts.title: 4 Pillars of OOP
concepts.summary: Encapsulation (bundling data and methods, hiding internals), Abstraction (hiding implementation details), Inheritance (reusing code), Polymorphism (many forms).

concepts.title: Overloading vs Overriding
concepts.summary: Overloading: Same method name with different parameters in same class (compile-time). Overriding: Subclass provides specific implementation of parent method (run-time).

concepts.title: Abstract Class vs Interface
concepts.summary: An abstract class can have state, constructors, and concrete methods. An interface specifies a contract (behavior) that implementing classes must satisfy.

concepts.title: SOLID Principles
concepts.summary: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, and Dependency Inversion.

interviewQuestions.question: Tell me about yourself and your journey in Computer Science.
interviewQuestions.strategy: Structure with Past -> Present -> Future: Introduce education background, highlight top technical skills/projects, and explain why this specific company aligns with your career goals.
interviewQuestions.sampleAnswer: I am a final-year student specializing in Computer Science. Over the last three years, I've focused on full-stack web development and core algorithmic problem solving. Recently, I built a Campus Placement Preparation Portal using React, which streamlined interview tracks and DSA drills for over 200 classmates. I am excited to bring my problem-solving mindset and full-stack capabilities to an innovative engineering team like yours.

interviewQuestions.question: Describe a challenging situation in a team project and how you resolved it.
interviewQuestions.strategy: Situation (Context), Task (Challenge), Action (What YOU did concretely), Result (Measurable outcome).
interviewQuestions.sampleAnswer: Situation: In our group semester project, we faced a major API mismatch 48 hours before submission between our React client and Express backend. Task: I needed to reconcile the schemas without delaying the milestone. Action: I organized a rapid 2-hour sync, drafted a clear JSON contract specification, and wrote adapter middlewares. Result: We integrated successfully ahead of schedule and secured the highest grade in the class.

interviewQuestions.question: What are your greatest strength and your biggest area for improvement?
interviewQuestions.strategy: Strength: Back with evidence. Weakness: State an authentic weakness along with active steps you are taking to overcome it.
interviewQuestions.sampleAnswer: My strength is disciplined consistency; I solve coding problems daily and have built a strong habit of writing clean, documented code. An area I'm actively improving is balancing perfectionism with delivery speed; I have adopted time-boxing techniques which helped me deliver quality features much faster.

interviewQuestions.question: Where do you see yourself in the next 3 to 5 years?
interviewQuestions.strategy: Demonstrate ambition, commitment to skill growth, and desire to take on technical ownership.
interviewQuestions.sampleAnswer: In 3 to 5 years, I envision myself as a solid end-to-end software engineer, mastering cloud architecture and taking ownership of key system modules. I also aim to mentor incoming junior developers and contribute meaningfully to architectural decisions.
